replies.author: NoahRaketic
replies.text:
pixel---fold Yeah, I tried it and got the same issue. Emailed Proton support and got this exchange:

Lumo fails to launch without "Native Code Debugging" permitted in settings. This is a sensitive permission that preferably wouldn't be required for the app to launch.

This is the official Android app from the Play Store.

Hi,

Thanks for reaching out.

This ensures automatic integrity validation and reduces the risk of modified builds being flagged by antivirus tools.

Kind regards,

Ibro

Proton Customer Support

Hi,

This response is a vague rationalization.

Other Android apps by Proton do not require ptrace to function, so do these apps not need integrity verification or to hide from AV tools that builds are modified?

What component's integrity is being verified? For the app's native code, the OS and Play Store are responsible for verifying that against the certificate. ptrace access is also not necessary to cryptographically verify remotely hosted code.

Best regards,

Noah

Hi Noah,

Other Proton apps don’t have integrity protection. The reason our app may be flagged by antivirus software is that we rely heavily on WebView for much of the app’s functionality, which can sometimes be perceived as suspicious behavior. This is less common in traditional apps, which typically don’t rely on WebView to the same extent.

Kind regards,

Ibro

Proton Customer Support

replies.author: 0xC0DED0D0
replies.text:
Can confirm. Proton Mail 7.11.10, in this case. Only happened once, so far.

As many are describing the same issue, with various applications, starting simultaneously and seemingly in correlation with a GrapheneOS update (202610210n?) I have these hypotheses:

• GrapheneOS failed in blocking native code debugging previously.

• The OS blocked them, but didn't notify. Notifications are working again since last update.

• GrapheneOS is now "overzealous" in it's blocking attempts, and warns of false positives.

No idea about probabilities for these, and there could be other non-OS related explanations, but the issue seems in order to be investigated.

I trust that the @GrapheneOS team is doing so. 👍
